name: Puligny-Montrachet

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.
keyfacts: Puligny-Montrachet is a Côte de Beaune commune in Burgundy, and more than 99% of its production is white wine.
There are four Grand Cru vineyards: Montrachet, Bâtard-Montrachet, Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet and Chevalier-Montrachet.
Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet cross the communal border and are shared with Chassagne-Montrachet.
Young white Puligny-Montrachet is pale gold with green glints, with floral, fruity, nutty and mineral notes and a honeyed touch.

notes: White Puligny-Montrachet is often very mineral, with more restrained oak than some other Côte de Beaune villages.
It is usually called elegant rather than fruit-driven, and it is steelier than Chassagne-Montrachet.

blurb.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making almost only white wine, from Chardonnay. It has four Grand Cru vineyards, with Montrachet the best known, and 17 Premier Crus.
